### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd ed.), §6.3 (printed p. 136, PDF p. 145), item `awodey:6.3:construction-boolean-exponential` — the unnumbered construction opening the Heyting-algebra section: any Boolean algebra, read as a poset category, has finite products (top and binary meet) and exponentials, so "Boolean algebra" generalizes to "cartesian closed poset". That is verbatim the general half (b) of this issue's Exercise 1, so no new issue is filed; the Boolean-algebra *structure* itself is Awodey's §2.2, already filed as #653, which this work should consume rather than redefine.

Awodey states the exponential in the explicit Boolean form rather than as an abstract relative pseudo-complement, and verifies it by two computations in the Boolean laws. That is a sharper deliverable than "the exponential is the relative pseudo-complement", so it gets its own line:

- [ ] (from Awodey §6.3) exhibit the Boolean exponential explicitly as the join of the complement of the antecedent with the consequent, and prove *both* of the book's verifications from the Boolean laws: the evaluation inequality (that object met with the antecedent lies below the consequent) and the transposition (from a meet inequality to an implication inequality)

Unchanged in-tree state as of the Awodey Chapter 6 pass, re-verified: `grep -rniI --include='*.v' 'BooleanAlgebra'` → 0 hits, and no complement or relative-complement operation exists anywhere; `Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:80` (`Two_Cartesian`, product is the meet) and `:98` (`Two_Terminal`) still give the two-element order its products and top with no `Cocartesian`, `Initial` or `Closed` companion — `Instance/Two/` contains only `Discrete.v` and `Monoidal.v`. The only thin cartesian *closed* instance in the tree remains `Instance/Props.v:94` (`Props_Closed`, `exponent_obj := Basics.impl`), which its own header at `:27` calls a Heyting **pre**algebra — an intuitionistic implication, not the Boolean formula, so it is a same-name-weaker witness for this item rather than a discharge of it. The generalization sentence itself still appears only as prose at `Instance/Two.v:85`–`:89`.

Note for sequencing: the Heyting-algebra class and the reusable "thin category + two-sided transposition ⇒ `Closed`" constructor are drafted as separate Awodey §6.3 issues; if they land first, both halves of this issue become instances of that constructor instead of hand-built `Closed` instances.
